parsing_rationale: The document describes the data model for a CLI To-Do Manager. I have mapped the 'Task' and 'Fields' sections to the Task Description, 'Validation Rules' and 'Operational Rules' to Constraints, and 'State Transitions' to the operational flow. Since this is a data model specification being treated as a 'task' doc type, I have extracted the field definitions and validation rules as the primary technical atoms (constraints and sub_tasks).

project_info.brief_explanation: Definition of the data structure, validation rules, and storage logic for a JSON-based task manager.

sections.title: Data Model: CLI To-Do List Manager
Task
sections.raw_content: Represents one to-do item stored in `~/.todos.json`.

sections.title: Fields
sections.raw_content:
- `id`: Integer, unique, sequential, positive, required
- `description`: String, required, trimmed, must not be empty
- `completed`: Boolean, required, defaults to `false`
- `created_at`: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp string, required, immutable after creation

sections.title: Validation Rules
sections.raw_content:
- `id` must be greater than zero and must not duplicate an existing task ID.
- `description` must contain non-whitespace content after trimming.
- `completed` must always be a boolean value.
- `created_at` must be present when the task is written and must not change during later updates.

sections.title: State Transitions
sections.raw_content:
- `pending` -> `completed` when the user runs `complete <id>`.
- `pending` -> `deleted` when the user runs `remove <id>`.
- `completed` -> `deleted` when the user runs `clear` or `remove <id>`

sections.title: Storage Model
sections.raw_content:
The JSON file contains an array of task objects.

Example:

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "description": "Buy groceries",
    "completed": false,
    "created_at": "2026-08-04T12:00:00Z"
  }
]
```

sections.title: Operational Rules
sections.raw_content:
- Missing storage file means an empty task list.
- Corrupted JSON must be treated as an error and reported to the user.
- IDs are assigned from the highest current ID plus one, even if earlier tasks were deleted.

elements.content: Implement the Task data model stored in ~/.todos.json
id: Integer, unique, sequential, positive, required (> 0, no duplicates)
completed: Boolean, required, defaults to false
created_at: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, required, immutable
Missing storage file must be treated as an empty task list
Corrupted JSON must be reported as an error to the user
IDs assigned from highest current ID + 1

Create a checklist for implementation (e.g., [ ] Implement JSON read/write, [ ] Implement ID increment logic).
